served.architecture: ModernBertForSequenceClassification, 5-class severity head (NONE/LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL) over a mean-pooled ModernBERT-large encoder, plus a shipped 1,000-point isotonic calibrator; 395,836,421 parameters, fp32
served.base_revision_note: SecJudge ships full fine-tuned weights, not an adapter, and its card names answerdotai/ModernBERT-large as the base without pinning a revision. No revision for the base repo appears anywhere in the published repo, so none is claimed here.
served.loader: the published secjudge_model.py forward path, driven directly on CPU; the repo's own load_secjudge() helper slices the input to 512 CHARACTERS before tokenising and was bypassed so the model saw the full 512 tokens it was trained for
served.prompting_contract: single serialised text (production_text rendering of the context variant); no policy, no question, no instruction -- NOT the Q0-Q4 judge grid
served.readout: severity argmax mapped to a disposition by the arm the model card specifies: NONE/LOW -> allow, MEDIUM -> confirm, HIGH/CRITICAL -> block. risk = 1 - P(allow) is SecJudge's own calibrated P(attack).

serving.device: CPU only: Intel Xeon 6975P-C, 8 physical cores, shared dev host. No GPU was used for any SecJudge stage.
serving.dtype_rationale: bfloat16 via AMX was measured at only 1.97x and broke agreement: is_attack agreement fell to 0.9375 and the calibrated score moved by up to 0.404, because the shipped isotonic calibrator has just 19 distinct output levels so tiny numeric shifts jump a whole plateau. fp32 was therefore used for every reported number.
serving.engine: PyTorch/transformers on CPU. SecJudge is an encoder classifier with a trained severity head, so no LLM serving engine applies.
serving.prefix_cache_reason: Not applicable: a single encoder forward pass per decision, so there is no prefix to reuse across tokens. A decision-level result cache was used and its hits are recorded in the stage throughput record.
serving.sharding: corpus shards, one resident fp32 model copy per shard process
serving.topology: 12 single-threaded CPU processes on 8 physical cores, fp32
serving.transport: in-process; no server, no port, no tunnel.
